solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Vegetable's beauty set down by artist

indicators.note: something set down by the artist is written after the artist's letters, so the second piece follows the first

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's stock artist
a dish is slang for an attractive person, a beauty

explanation.surface: A painter is credited with depicting a lovely vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp red root eaten raw in salads, a common vegetable.

clue.text: Call on team near to fighting

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the telephone
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A manager phones the squad shortly before a bout begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringside seats are those at the edge of a boxing ring, closest to the bout.

clue.text: Dead poser masquerading as bandit

indicators.note: something masquerading is in disguise, so the letters of the two words take on a new form

explanation.surface: A man feigning death turns out to be an outlaw in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masquerading' rearranges the nine letters of DEAD POSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw of the Wild West, a bandit or gunman.

clue.text: Phonecard conceals expensive weapon

indicators.note: one piece hides another inside it, so the card's letters wrap round the second word's synonym

parts.note: a SIM card is the card inside a mobile phone
dear means costly, expensive

explanation.surface: A costly gun is smuggled inside a mobile phone card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Phonecard' suggests a calling card for payphones, but here it is the small card inside a mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a pistol or other weapon carried at the belt.

clue.text: Colour of suit captured by writer

indicators.note: the second piece is held inside the writing tool, which surrounds it

parts.note: a pen is the tool one writes with
to suit is to be agreeable, as in 'that will agree with me'

explanation.surface: An author records the shade of a set of clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing, which fits the colour surface, but it is the verb meaning to be agreeable; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea-green is a light yellowish green shade, the hue of fresh peas.

clue.text: It shows one's intended to employ tutoring heartlessly

parts.note: to engage someone is to hire or employ them

indicators.note: without its heart, the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: mentoring is guiding or tutoring a younger person

explanation.surface: Something proves a person plans to hire coaching, done without warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' removes the middle O of MENTORING to leave MENTRING. 'intended' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning fiancé.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal band is worn to show that the wearer has a fiancé or fiancée, an intended partner.

clue.text: Large ice endlessly slipping?

indicators.note: slipping letters slide out of place, so they are rearranged
without its end, the last letter of the word for frozen water goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big mass of ice slides on without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts ICE to IC; 'slipping' rearranges LARGE plus IC. The whole clue also describes the answer, a huge sheet of ice creeping slowly downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacier is a huge mass of ice that moves slowly down a valley under its own weight.

clue.text: Be way out including touch of scattiness

indicators.note: the first piece contains the second inside it

parts.note: an exit is a way out of a building

indicators.note: a touch of something is a small amount, here just the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A slightly scatterbrained person is told to be very unconventional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts S, from 'touch of scattiness', inside EXIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being.

clue.text: Weapon cocked, go for small piece

indicators.note: something cocked is tilted or turned, and in a down clue that turns the word upside down

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
to go for something is to fetch or get it

explanation.surface: With the gun cocked, a gangster decides to grab a bit of the loot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocked' turns GUN into NUG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump, such as a nugget of gold.

clue.text: Dotty conveners set out to ostracise

indicators.note: the letters are laid out afresh, rearranged

explanation.surface: Crazy meeting organisers arrange to exclude someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'set out' rearranges all fourteen letters of DOTTY CONVENERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone to Coventry is a British idiom meaning to refuse to speak to them, to shun them.

clue.text: In positive signal, Stock Exchange initially moved slowly forward

indicators.note: the following letters go inside the nod

parts.note: a nod of the head signals yes

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Share prices crept upward after a hopeful sign on the trading floor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stock Exchange surface suggests shares edging upward; the definition really describes a car or boat creeping ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to edge ahead carefully, as a car noses into traffic.

clue.text: English ranting shown in print

parts.note: raving means talking wildly, ranting

explanation.surface: An Englishman's tirade appears in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shown in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An engraving is a picture printed from an engraved plate, a print.

clue.text: Saint's recompense getting tip off servant

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: losing its tip, the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a reward is a recompense

explanation.surface: A holy man's payment is withheld from a domestic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting tip off' removes the R of REWARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant who serves, on a ship or plane or in a great house.

clue.text: Bit of roast leg, it's thrown out

definitions.text: Bit of roast leg, it's thrown out

indicators.note: letters thrown out are scattered and rearranged
a bit of the word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Part of a joint of lamb is discarded at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown out' rearranges R (from 'Bit of roast') with LEG and ITS. Read whole, the clue describes the tough bit of meat left on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Gristle is the tough cartilage in meat, the bit of a joint a diner leaves.

clue.text: Film Grand National winner set to make return, holding form

indicators.note: the reversed string holds the next word inside it
the horse and the word for set are read backwards together

parts.note: Red Rum won the Grand National, Britain's great steeplechase, three times in the 1970s
laid means set down, as a table is laid
taken as written

explanation.surface: A famous racehorse is lined up for a comeback, holding its old form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make return' reverses REDRUMLAID to DIALMURDER; 'holding' puts FORM inside it after DIALM. Red Rum is a famous British racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dial M for Murder is a 1954 Alfred Hitchcock thriller.

clue.text: I led a riot, anarchic leader

indicators.note: anarchic means lawless and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rebel confesses to heading a lawless uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anarchic' rearranges I LED A RIOT; 'leader' looks like a person but is a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the editor's opinion column, the paper's lead article.

clue.text: It'll help cook get grime scrubbed

indicators.note: scrubbing works the letters over, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A kitchen tip: scrub away the dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrubbed' rearranges GET GRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass times the boiling of eggs, a gadget helping in the kitchen.

clue.text: Lazy fellow gets benefit free

parts.note: good means benefit, as in 'for your own good'
for nothing means free of charge

explanation.surface: An idler claims his welfare payment without paying anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A good-for-nothing is a worthless idle person, a layabout.

clue.text: Historical garment, cotton in the middle?

definitions.meaning: a close-fitting jacket worn by men in the 15th to 17th centuries
the central letters of the word cotton are a pair of Ts, read as a cryptic description

explanation.surface: Old clothing is made with cotton at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: the middle of 'cotton' is TT, which is spoken as 'double T'.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is the padded jacket worn by men in Tudor and Elizabethan times.

clue.text: Storm — sort endlessly overcome by former Blairite minister

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits on top of the second
without its end, the last letter of the word goes

parts.note: a type is a sort or kind
Geoff Hoon was Defence Secretary in Tony Blair's government

explanation.surface: A political tempest engulfs an ex-cabinet member.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'overcome by' places the first piece above the minister. Geoff Hoon served under Tony Blair.
explanation.definitionFit: A typhoon is a violent tropical cyclone of the western Pacific, a storm.

clue.text: American boss in marathon chosen

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A US company chief has been picked for a long-distance race.
explanation.definitionFit: Honcho is American slang for the person in charge, from Japanese for squad leader.

clue.text: Dim former pupil's treatment

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil, and the 's adds S
a cure is a remedy or treatment

explanation.surface: An old schoolmate's remedy is unclear.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, old boy, is the British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure means dim or dark, hard to see.

clue.text: Louvre embraces new point of view

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a louvre is a set of slats in a shutter, so one slat

explanation.surface: The Paris gallery welcomes a fresh perspective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Louvre' looks like the Paris museum but is a slatted shutter; 'embraces' puts N inside SLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A slant is a particular angle or bias on a subject, a point of view.

clue.text: Harmony left behind tuneless music

indicators.note: the word for left comes after the music

parts.note: rap is spoken rhythmic music without melody
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Harmony is lost when tuneless music remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb but gives PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious understanding between people.

clue.text: Cleaner part of South Africa turned rogue

parts.note: a char or charwoman is a British cleaner

indicators.note: the province's name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: Natal is a province of South Africa

explanation.surface: A domestic help from KwaZulu turns out to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses NATAL to LATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a fraud who claims skills he lacks, a rogue.

clue.text: Dislike one-day international's first pair of umpires

parts.note: ODI is the cricket abbreviation for a one-day international match

indicators.note: only the opening two letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: Cricket fans resent the first two officials at a limited-overs match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first pair of umpires' gives UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or strong disapproval.

clue.text: Lasts longer than unfashionable underwear

parts.note: out means out of fashion
stays are a corset, old-fashioned underwear

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned corsets outlive their era.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstay is to remain longer than someone or something else.

clue.text: One tries to catch old Englishman with Queen

parts.note: the Angles were a Germanic people who settled England
R is short for Regina, queen

explanation.surface: An Anglo-Saxon and the monarch go hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is a fisherman, who tries to catch fish.
